ruleset.name: tartine
ruleset.description:
Tartine's bug/security gate (pre-commit and CI). PMD stands in for SonarLint: there is no Sonar server or token here, so the same class of finding is enforced locally.
Enabled: PMD's errorprone and security categories, restricted to priority 3 (medium) or higher by the Gradle pmd task. These are the rules that flag likely bugs and vulnerabilities, not formatting.
Excluded, with reasons (all are style/design or false positives in this codebase, not bugs or security): * AvoidDuplicateLiterals - DRY guideline; opcode/descriptor literals repeat by nature in a DEX translator. * AvoidLiteralsInIfCondition - readability only; comparing against opcode and constant values is the point of the translator. * DoNotHardCodeSDCard - flags the guest VFS's own /sdcard mount path, which is not host storage. * UseProperClassLoader - J2EE-specific; this is a desktop host. * NullAssignment - clearing fields/locals is intentional here. * AvoidCatchingGenericException - the translator catches broadly to degrade an unresolved guest method to its named gap. * AvoidFieldNameMatchingMethodName - naming only. * AvoidAccessibilityAlteration - setAccessible IS the reflection bridge and the probe harness (guest/ and Main); it is sandboxed. * ReturnEmptyCollectionRatherThanNull - GuestFiles mirrors java.io.File.list, whose contract is null when not a directory. * AvoidBranchingStatementAsLastInLoop - style only. * AssignmentInOperand - `while ((pos = next()) != -1)` is the deliberate cursor idiom in the binary parsers. * AvoidInstanceofChecksInCatchClause - style only; the multi-catch rewrite adds no safety here.
CloseResource stays on, but limited to genuinely ownerless resources (IO streams, the JDK file manager, executors, java.util streams). The gfx seam, Skija natives and GLFW callbacks are owned by a field, a caller or a singleton, and peekPixels()/static-font aliasing makes the default AutoCloseable sweep pure false positives.
Its allowedResourceTypes keeps PMD's defaults (in-memory byte/char streams need no close) plus two entries: * java.nio.file.FileSystem - the system jrt: filesystem; closing it breaks the JVM. * java.lang.Process - the host theme probes and the Windows junction helper drain and waitFor the child; Process.close() only exists from a JDK newer than our release-21 floor, so destroy() is the most these paths can do, and there is nothing left to release.
EmptyCatchBlock keeps its default severity but allows blocks that hold only a comment: the translator and the JDK scanner deliberately swallow unresolved-type/lookup failures, and the comment records why.
Everything else in those two categories is a gate.
